---
title: "Figure 3—figure supplement 3 — residual autocorrelation: the gating memory LSE and NR leave in the data, and that R and IR whiten"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
THE DATA-LEVEL VERSION of Figure 3's row F. Row F plots the autocorrelation of the SCORE (an
inference-level object); this plots the autocorrelation of the standardised RESIDUAL r_std =
(patch_current - y_mean)/sqrt(y_var), which is an observable of the data against the fitted mean and
needs no likelihood to read. figure_3.Rmd's own note flagged this as the panel that "stays in the full
figure_3"; here it is, on the merged-paper roster LSE / NR / R / IR.

WHY IT IS A GATING-NOISE INDICATOR (Luciano's point). The recorded current is gating fluctuation
(temporally correlated: the channel population relaxes over a finite time) plus instrumental noise
(white). So the residual autocorrelation at lag k is

    rho_resid(k) = rho_gating(k) * V_gate / (V_gate + V_inst),

the gating autocorrelation times the gating fraction of the variance. It is large when gating
dominates and falls to zero as instrumental noise drowns it — a direct read of how much gating signal
is present, from the data alone.

WHAT EACH ALGORITHM'S r_std MEASURES, and why the ACF is NOT the same object across the row. y_var is
the variance the algorithm CLAIMS. LSE claims one global marginalised variance (no gating term), so it
divides the raw residual by a constant and its r_std ACF is the gating ACF itself, undistorted — the
cleanest estimate of rho_gating(k) available. NR claims a per-time diagonal variance but still models
no temporal structure, so it too retains the off-diagonal memory. R and IR condition the prediction on
the past, so a correctly specified model has already absorbed the gating correlation and their r_std
ACF should be WHITE. The gap between the LSE/NR curves and the R/IR curves is exactly what the
recursion buys: not more information, a residual with no memory left in it.

CAVEAT, one cell. These dumps are a single design point (the figure_3_time cell, noise 0.1, the
gating-dominated regime). So this shows the CONTRAST between algorithms at fixed noise, where gating is
strong and the LSE/NR memory is at its most visible. The noise SWEEP of rho_resid(1) — the actual
gating-fraction indicator across the design space — would need this residual ACF emitted per battery
cell, or time-resolved dumps at several noise levels; neither exists yet. Flagged, not silently
implied.

RENDER: reads the four ~1 GB dumps ONE AT A TIME (only the r_std rows, only the columns needed), so
peak memory stays near one dump, not four. Run where figures/data/ resolves.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)
```

```{r params}
ALGOS  <- c("LSE", "NR", "R", "IR")
ALAB   <- c(LSE = "LSE", NR = "NR", R = "R", IR = "IR")
COL    <- c(LSE = "#B2182B", NR = "#D6604D", R = "#4393C3", IR = "#053061")  # naive pair warm, recursive cool
LAGMAX <- 20
```

```{r compute}
# ACF of one recording's residual series, ordered in time by sample_index (verified: sample_index is
# the time step, monotone in step_middle at fixed 1 ms spacing, 100 steps/recording). Post-agonist
# only would be cleaner, but the pre-agonist steps have r_std ~ 0 derivatives and drop out of acf()
# scaling; we keep the whole trace and note it. mean over recordings, +/- 1.96 SE per lag.
acf_one <- function(x) if (length(x) > LAGMAX + 1) as.numeric(acf(x, lag.max = LAGMAX, plot = FALSE)$acf) else rep(NA_real_, LAGMAX + 1)

read_resid_acf <- function(a) {
  dt <- fread(sprintf("../data/figure_3_time_dlik_%s.csv", a), skip = 1, showProgress = FALSE,
              select = c("component_path", "calculus", "simulation_index", "sample_index", "value"))
  rr <- dt[component_path == "r_std" & calculus == "primitive" & !is.na(sample_index)]
  rm(dt); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  # the writer emits every (sim,sample) row TWICE (blank-segment + segment-0 copies); collapse by mean
  rr <- rr[, .(r = mean(value)), by = .(simulation_index, sample_index)]
  rr <- rr[is.finite(r)][order(simulation_index, sample_index)]
  M  <- rr[, .(acf = list(acf_one(r))), by = simulation_index]
  A  <- do.call(rbind, M$acf[!sapply(M$acf, function(v) all(is.na(v)))])
  rm(rr, M); gc(verbose = FALSE)
  tibble(algo = a, lag = 0:LAGMAX, acf = colMeans(A, na.rm = TRUE),
         se = apply(A, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(A)))
}

acf_resid <- map_dfr(ALGOS, read_resid_acf) %>%
  mutate(algo = factor(algo, levels = ALGOS)) %>% filter(lag >= 1)

# the one-number summary: lag-1 residual autocorrelation per algorithm
cat("residual autocorrelation at lag 1 (the gating-fraction indicator, this cell):\n")
print(as.data.frame(acf_resid %>% filter(lag == 1) %>% select(algo, acf, se)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2}
ggplot(acf_resid, aes(lag, acf, colour = algo, fill = algo)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = .4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = acf - 1.96 * se, ymax = acf + 1.96 * se), colour = NA, alpha = .18) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .7) + geom_point(size = 1.1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COL, labels = ALAB, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COL, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, LAGMAX, 5)) +
  labs(x = "lag (time steps)", y = expression("residual autocorrelation  " * rho[resid](k)),
       title = "Gating memory in the residual: retained by LSE and NR, whitened by R and IR") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.88, 0.8), plot.title = element_text(size = 9))
ggsave("Figure_3_supplement_3.pdf", width = 7.0, height = 4.2)
```
